title: Oncall signal priority and noise suppression — compact wireframe + backlog
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of UX ideas and a lightweight wireframe for prioritizing oncall signals, reducing noisy notifications, and surfacing SLO-relevant alerts to the right stakeholders. This is an exploratory doc to align product, SRE, and solutions on pragmatic controls we can ship in the console within a small sprint (2–3 weeks).

Problem statement / context:
- Teams are overwhelmed by alert noise: duplicate signals across tiers, infra vs. product noise, and chatty third-party checks.
- Current console lets you configure channels and thresholds but lacks a compact way to: 1) prioritize signals by impact on SLOs, 2) suppress duplicates across detectors, and 3) route degraded-but-degrading signals differently from hard failures.
- Goal: Add lightweight primitives in Console that let users define: impact label (SLO-critical | user-facing | informational), dedupe group rules, and a suppression/fallback matrix for channels.

Key constraints / design goals:
- Minimal friction: defaults that work for most teams; advanced rules behind an "Advanced" toggle.
- Observable outcomes: any routing/suppression should have an immediate, visible "what would happen" simulation view in the UI.
- Tenant-aware: per-customer policies (for dedicated/private) but also org-global policies for hosted.
- Safe-by-default: no silent drops without a visible audit/trail and an easy revert button.

Users & personas:
- Oncall engineer (primary): wants fewer pages, clearer signal prioritization.
- Platform owner: wants consistency across services; needs templated policies.
- Product engineer: wants to hear only user-facing degradations.
- Incident commander: wants fast switch to noisy-mode (expand channels) during major incidents.

Wireframe (compact, ascii sketch to communicate flow quickly):

[Alert Rule editor — top half]
Name: [text]              Impact: (SLO-critical v user-facing v informational) [o]SLO-critical [ ]user-facing [ ]info
Sources: [service detector, latency monitor, external-probe]  Deduplicate group: [dropdown or regex] 
Thresholds: [value / op]   Rolling window: [5m / 10m / 1h]

[Priority + channel matrix — bottom half]
Impact  | Severity  | Primary channel  | Backup channel | Suppress if duplicate in last X | Escalation window
SLO-critical | P1 | PagerDuty (team-oncall) | Email (team) | 60s | 10m
user-facing  | P2 | Slack (#prod-alerts)      | Email (team) | 300s | 30m
informational | P3 | Slack (#dev-notifs)      | none        | 1200s | N/A

[Behaviour toggles (right column)]:
- Dedup across detectors: ON/OFF
- Auto-silence flapping signals: percentage threshold
- Simulation: "Run against 7-day history" button -> shows if rule would have fired and what channels triggered

Example flows / micro-scenarios:
1) Latency spike on embeddings service (SLO-critical): two detectors fire (latency monotonic and synthetic probe). With dedupe group configured, only one PagerDuty page happens and Slack gets a summarized thread. If PagerDuty is down, fallback to Email.
2) Third-party healthcheck flapping: policy suggests marking source as informational and suppressing repeat events for 15m after the first occurrence.
3) Major incident toggle: admin can flip Console to "broadcast" mode, temporarily disabling suppression and expanding channel fanout for 1h.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should default dedupe windows be? 60s vs 5m will impact both noise and detection latency. (Proposal: default 120s with documentation and org-level override.)
- Simulation accuracy: should we run the user's live routing engine against historical events in a sandbox, or approximate? Sandbox gives higher confidence but more backend work.
- UX for per-tenant policy templates vs. ad-hoc rules: templates help on-boarding but may hide nuance. We need a template marketplace or import/export.
- Permission model: who can flip "broadcast" mode? only org admins or also SRE? Provide an audit trail.

Backlog (proposed small-scope slices for MVP, ordered):
- RW-2562: Dedup group field + basic dedupe engine (default 120s) -> UI: add dropdown/regex + tooltip (owner: Miguel).
- RW-2563: Impact label field + channel default mapping (SLO-critical -> Pager) + simple channel matrix UI (owner: Claire).
- RW-2564: Simulation view (run against N days of events) — UI placeholder + backend simulator (owner: Samir).
- RW-2571: Broadcast mode toggle + audit log entry + rollout guard (owner: Aisha).
- RW-2588: Advanced suppression rules: flapping detection and auto-silence (owner: eng-SRE collaboration).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can create/edit rules with an Impact label, Dedup group, and a channel matrix mapping.
- Simulation shows a list of historical events that would have been suppressed, deduped, or rerouted (summary table).
- Audit entries created for any rule toggles and broadcast mode flips.
- Defaults applied reduce median alert pages/day for a sample org by >20% in internal experiment (measured).

Design notes & copy suggestions:
- Impact label tooltip: "SLO-critical: affects core user-facing SLOs. Use for pages. User-facing: visible to customers but non-critical. Informational: telemetry/logs, no pages."
- Dedup tooltip: "Group detectors that signal the same underlying issue (e.g. latency monotonic + synthetic probe). Matches are by service name + regex on metric name by default."
- Simulation button copy: "Preview routing: show historical outcomes"

Implementation hints for PM/Eng handoff:
- Reuse existing routing engine code path for channel resolution; add a toggle to run in 'simulate' mode that does not produce side effects.
- Store dedupe groups as light-weight rules (name + matchers + dedupe window) — keep simple for MVP.
- Ensure audit log entries are human-readable and include 'would have been suppressed' notes from simulation runs.

Next steps / meeting ask:
- Quick sync with SRE and console frontend (30m) to validate dedupe semantics and feasibility of simulation run (ask: Miguel, Claire, Samir).
- UX sketch session (30m) to iterate on the compact matrix layout and mobile behavior.
- Wire up a Linear epic and break into the backlog items above; link to the PR above when prototype UI is available.

Notes to self (TODO):
- Draft a short survey for a few beta customers to measure perceived noise after defaults applied.
- Add a short help doc for "broadcast mode" governance.
- Capture edge cases for third-party checkers that should always escalate despite dedupe (webhook origin allowlist).

End of doc.
notes_short: Draft UX + backlog for compact oncall signal prioritization, dedupe groups, and suppression matrix with simulation view. Targets an MVP of dedupe+impact+simulation.
